# Differential cases for the line readers of G3's olympia/z.c and the field
# scan and print helpers of olympia/io.c, at G3
# aa68d137729564cfcd2e91c808c38f3e76d65744.
#
# tools/io-compat/run.sh feeds this file to a C driver built from the
# pinned sources and records its output in io-c-output.txt; TestIOMatchesC
# feeds it to the Go port and requires the same output.
#
# Each "section NAME" line starts a section. Every section runs in a fresh
# process (a fresh world, after glob_init()) in a fresh, empty directory, so
# a section may end in a crash, and the files it writes are its own. run.sh
# adds "exit STATUS" after each section. stderr goes to the same place as
# stdout, in order.
#
# One operation per line; a line that starts with '#' is a comment, and
# blank lines are skipped. N, K, SK, P and V are integers, read with
# strtol(s, NULL, 0) and stored in a C int. TEXT is the rest of the line
# after one space, with \xHH and \\ escapes; with no space it is empty.
# NAME is one word. Strings print with bytes outside ' '..'~', and '\', as
# \xHH, and NULL prints as NULL.
#
# The driver holds an ilist L, a sparse K, a skill_ents_list, an
# item_ents_list, a trades_list, a req_ents_list, an entity_player (for
# its admits) and an olytime, all empty at the start of a section.
#
#   alloc N K SK        alloc_box(N, K, SK)
#   setname N TEXT      set_name(N, TEXT)
#   namen N K TEXT      set_name(N, TEXT repeated K times)
#   pretty P            pretty_data_files = P
#   extbox N            ext_boxnum = N
#   put NAME TEXT       append TEXT to file NAME
#   putn NAME K TEXT    append TEXT to file NAME, K times
#   readfile NAME       readfile(NAME), and its result
#   closefile NAME      closefile(NAME)
#   readlin             readlin()
#   readlin_ew          readlin_ew()
#   skip K              readlin() K times
#   drain               readlin() until it returns NULL; prints the count
#                       of lines and the last one
#   fopen NAME          fopen(NAME, "r") for getlin
#   getlin              getlin() of that file
#   getlin_ew           getlin_ew() of that file
#   ew TEXT             eat_leading_trailing_whitespace(TEXT)
#   hash TEXT           linehash(TEXT) and t_string(TEXT)
#   next                line = readlin(), then past its first byte if that
#                       is white space, as the entity scanners do; prints
#                       line, linehash(line) and t_string(line)
#
# The scan operations pass t_string(line) to the helper, as the entity
# scanners do, and print what they scanned into:
#
#   box_scan                 box_scan()
#   boxlist_scan N           boxlist_scan(t, N, &L)
#   boxlist0_scan N          boxlist0_scan(t, N, &L)
#   ilist_scan               ilist_scan(t, &L)
#   known_scan N             known_scan(t, &K, N)
#   admit_scan N             admit_scan(t, N, player)
#   skill_scan N             skill_list_scan(t, &skills, N)
#   item_scan N              item_list_scan(t, &items, N)
#   trade_scan N             trade_list_scan(t, &trades, N)
#   req_scan N               req_list_scan(t, &reqs, N)
#   olytime_scan             olytime_scan(t, &olytime)
#
# The print operations print to stdout, with TEXT as the header:
#
#   box_print N TEXT         box_print()
#   boxlist_print TEXT       boxlist_print() of L
#   boxlist0_print TEXT      boxlist0_print() of L
#   ilist_print TEXT         ilist_print() of L
#   known_print TEXT         known_print() of K, then K (which it sorts)
#   admit_print              admit_print() of the player
#   skill_print TEXT         skill_list_print()
#   item_print TEXT          item_list_print()
#   trade_print TEXT         trade_list_print()
#   req_print TEXT           req_list_print()
#   olytime_print TEXT       olytime_print()
#
# and these set what they print:
#
#   set V...                 L = V...
#   setk V...                K = V...
#   skill SKILL KNOW DAYS EXP     append a skill_ent
#   item ITEM QTY                 append an item_ent
#   trade KIND ITEM QTY COST CLOAK LEFT MONTH EXPIRE   append a trade
#   req ITEM QTY CONSUME          append a req_ent
#   admit TARG SENSE V...         append an admit
#   olytime TURN DAY DAYS         set the olytime
#   zero WHERE ALLOC         zero_check() of a struct loc_info with where
#                            WHERE and, if ALLOC, an empty but allocated
#                            here_list
#
# Out of scope, because C is undefined there: a skill or req line with too
# few numbers (uninitialized locals), and a skill, item, trade or req entry
# that is empty (s[strlen(s)-1] reads before the string). readlin() before
# any readfile() crashes in C (point is NULL); the engine always calls
# readfile() first.

section readlin plain lines
put f one\x0a\x0atwo  \x0a\x09three\x09\x0a  \x0d\x0alast
readfile f
readlin

readlin
